rule: How many residents of each building commute, and by which mode
source: S7 homes: census 2021 by tract, corrected once for working from home

rule: When residents leave for work and when workers arrive, by mode
source: S7: census 2021 hour bands by tract (98-10-0480, 98-10-0504)

rule: The streets a person may walk, and the doors out of the area
Which buildings hold business premises, and how many
How much can be seen from each walkable street
Residents who walk to work outside the area head for Place Ville Marie, through the door of the area that makes the whole walk shortest
source: downtown holds most of the jobs within walking distance; no open table says where Griffintown's walkers work
replace_with: census commuting flows by tract (not open)

rule: The share of resident walkers who work inside the area is the number of people who walk to work here divided by the residents who walk to work (q)
source: assumes everyone who walks to a job here lives here, so q is an upper bound
replace_with: a survey of where residents work

rule: Inside the area, workers go to the buildings with business premises, in proportion to their number of premises
source: premises are counted on the tax roll; jobs per premises are not open

rule: Riders walk to the metro entrance or bus stop nearest their home along S1
source: S7 measures it; nothing says which stop people choose

rule: Workers who arrive by metro or bus come from the entrance or stop nearest their workplace
Departures and arrivals spread evenly inside each census band; a walk falls in the hour it starts (residents) or ends (workers)
source: the census gives bands only; most walks here last under 20 minutes
replace_with: counts by quarter hour per trip

rule: A walker who passes through a junction is counted there once
source: the city counts crossings per crosswalk; a walker may cross none, one or two

rule: Only the walks counted above happen: no errands, school runs, dog walks, visitors, or walks from parking
source: this slice holds commuters only; the rest is what the counts can show is missing

rule: Stops and doors are chosen by the shortest walk in every reading, so the readings differ only in the route
source: one rule changed at a time keeps the comparison readable

rule: Reading 'open': enclosed streets feel longer, cost = length x (1 + 0.5 x (1 - rank of area seen)); a street S8 did not measure counts as middling
source: a hypothesis drawn from isovist studies, not a finding; the weight 0.5 is a choice tried at 0.25 and 1 in the stress tests

rule: Reading 'straight': walkers take the route with the fewest degrees of turning
source: Hillier and Iida (2005) found least-angle routes fit observed movement better than shortest ones in London

rule: Train, bicycle, car and other commuters do not walk in this slice
source: their walks to a station or a car are short or unknown
